p: One of the joys of karting is that it works for groups where nobody's at the same level. The petrolhead in your crew and the mate who's never driven anything faster than a supermarket trolley can share a track and both have a brilliant time, because lap timing lets everyone race against themselves as well as each other.

That said, if your group is very mixed, have a chat with staff when you book about the best session format. Some groups prefer a relaxed first session to get the feel of things before the serious racing starts.

Keep things friendly on track. Leave space when you overtake, don't divebomb people who are still finding their feet and give a thumbs up to whoever beats you. The banter in the cafe afterwards is better when nobody's sulking.
If someone in the group doesn't want to drive at all, check whether there's space for them to watch from the side. Cheering on mates is half the fun.

Fancy something completely different afterwards? The RAF Museum London over in Colindale is free to visit and packed with historic aircraft, which suits anyone still buzzing from the speed. Brent Cross Shopping Centre is close by for food and a mooch round the shops, and it's easy to reach by car from the North Circular and the M1.
